doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The need for jazz history and scholarship courses
summary: Brown suggests jazz scholarship courses and Burrell asks him to put it in writing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: You mentioned earlier—off mic that— the importance of jazz scholarship. I was fortunate when I went to Rutgers. That was the first class they were offering a Masters in Music, but du- while the time I was there they also instituted a master- or a degree in jazz studies, so it was more jazz scholarship looking at. Is that on the horizon for here as well?

Well, yes, I would- I would say [pause]…I can’t be specific about it. I- I understand what you’re saying and, um [pause]…I don’t know how to say this: what I, what I would like to see is more courses in jazz history…

… So people will really understand the depth and the bigger picture. You know, what we’re teaching is how to perform, how to write music, but we’re not teaching the big picture. And I would like to see that and I’m going to take your question as a suggestion that we, we look into that more.

Particularly since you have the affiliation or (are) under the auspices of ethnomusicology, which has a, you know, it definitely has a- a discipline, and jazz of course would- is ideally suited for that as opposed to musicology…
Right. Brown:…where you’re looking at the cultural context of the music…
Right. Brown:…And you’re understand the music and it- its role in culture.

Now this is something you’ve been talking about for the duration of this- of this interview. It’s obviously something that you hold near and dear: understanding where this music comes from; what are the values that have been invested in this music.
So I’m just wondering if that’s some- you know, something that you’re able to bring into this very, you know, growing but ultimately comprehensive…
…but hopefully I w- hopefully we can. I hope we can. Yeah.
Um-hm. ‘Cause you’ve got great, great instructors and professors here…
…that are very, very versed in that so…
…it- it’d be great to be able to offer that as well ‘cause I think that that would make yours’, you know, the program here, you know, the leading program…
Because of the emphasis you have on, on the performance already now, composition and then scholarship…
I think you’re right…I’ll take that as a very strong suggestion…

..and in fact I would even ask you to put something in writing to that effect, so not only can I be reminded of your comments, but I can share it with some other people to remind them of the tracks we should follow. [laughs]
That’s a very thoughtful and- suggestion and coming from you I think it would
But again I- that’s only- the inspiration for that was just hearing you talk about the music.
…but you, you, you’re bouncing back at me with that suggestion. I would seriously like you to put something in writing for that…
